manual.title: The Birthday Party Field Manual
manual.subtitle: Planning, hosting and surviving a party for twelve seven-year-olds
manual.voice: A retired army logistics officer and father of three who has run twenty-two children’s parties and writes about them exactly as he once wrote operational orders: clipped, numbered, deadpan. Party day is H-hour, guests are “the twelve”, the cake is “the objective” and the host is addressed as “Party Lead”. Every instruction is a concrete figure — sausages per child, minutes per game, adults per head. The military framing is a dry joke he never winks at, and through it shows real warmth and a good grasp of how seven-year-olds think, tire and fall apart. Short declarative sentences, the occasional one-line aside. Absolutely unbending about allergies, water near children, choking hazards and the headcount: every child goes home to the right adult.
